title: Aloo Matar Bhaji

ingredients.title: For the Curry
items: Potatoes – 3 medium (about 400 g), peeled and diced into ½-inch cubes
Green peas – 1 cup, fresh or frozen
Oil – 2 tbsp, mustard oil or vegetable oil
Water – 2–3 tbsp, plus extra if needed

ingredients.title: For the Ground Spices
items: Red chili powder – ½ tsp, adjust to taste

ingredients.title: For Finishing
items: Fresh coriander leaves – 1 tbsp, finely chopped

instruction.title: Prep the Ingredients
steps: Peel and dice the potatoes into even ½-inch cubes for uniform cooking.
If using frozen peas, soak them in warm water for 5–10 minutes, then drain.
Measure and prepare all spices and ingredients before cooking.

instruction.title: Temper & Sauté the Aromatics
steps: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
If using mustard oil, heat it until it reaches smoking point, then reduce the heat slightly.
Add cumin seeds and optional mustard seeds and allow them to crackle.
Add the slit green chili and chopped onion.
Sauté for 5–6 minutes until the onion becomes golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for about 1 minute until the raw aroma disappears.

instruction.title: Prepare the Spice Base
steps: Add the chopped tomato and cook until softened and the oil begins to separate.
Add turmeric, coriander powder, and red chili powder.
Stir well and cook for 1–2 minutes to bloom the spices.

instruction.title: Cook the Potatoes & Peas
steps: Add the diced potatoes and stir thoroughly to coat them with the masala.
Add green peas, salt, and 2–3 tbsp water.
Mix gently and cover the pan.
Cook over low-medium heat for 12–15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add a small splash of water only if needed to prevent the masala from sticking or burning.
Cook until the potatoes are tender but still hold their shape.

instruction.title: Final Seasoning
steps: Sprinkle garam masala over the cooked potatoes and peas.
Stir gently to distribute the spice without breaking the potatoes.
Cook uncovered for another 2–3 minutes to allow slight crisping at the base.

instruction.title: Finish & Serve
steps: Turn off the heat.
Add lemon juice if using and sprinkle with fresh coriander.
Add a pinch of amchur or crushed kasuri methi if desired.
Serve hot with phulka, chapati, poori, or steamed rice.

chefTips: Oil: Mustard oil gives the bhaji a more traditional North Indian flavor; heat it to smoking point before cooking.
Tanginess: Add a pinch of amchur or a squeeze of fresh lemon juice for a brighter finish.
Kasuri methi: Crushed dried fenugreek leaves added at the end provide extra depth and aroma.
Texture: Avoid excessive stirring once the potatoes are tender so they remain intact instead of breaking down.
Water: Keep this preparation relatively dry; add only enough water to cook the potatoes without making a gravy.
Peas: Fresh peas provide excellent texture, while frozen peas are convenient and work well when properly thawed.
